info.title: Teletalk One — channel API
info.summary: The contract the management portal is built against.
info.description:
Published as JSON rather than YAML so that `scripts/check-contract.mjs` can read it with no dependency at all; any tool will convert it. It is generated from nothing and generates one thing: `src/lib/apiRoutes.ts`. That file is the client's only source of paths, and CI fails if it drifts from this document — which is what makes the contract a file rather than a convention.

Three rules below are load-bearing and must survive into the real service:

1. **Capabilities, not roles.** `/auth/session` returns a capability set. Teletalk's real hierarchy is then a server-side change, not a frontend release.
2. **Server-owned display strings are `{bn, en}`.** If BVS/CBS/DMS return English only, every screen is mixed-language no matter how well the client is built.
3. **Mutations honour `Idempotency-Key`.** The client queues transactions offline and retries them under the original key. If the server performs the work twice on a replayed key, the customer is charged twice. This is the single most important line in this document.

post.description: One endpoint for all five SIM flows; `kind` selects. The client may submit this minutes after the retailer pressed the button, from a queue, under the original `Idempotency-Key`.

200.description: Accepted by CBS. A replayed Idempotency-Key MUST return this same body without performing the work again.

get.summary: Lifting requests this session may see
get.description: **The server MUST scope this to the session's role, zone and territory.** A dealer must never receive another dealer's demand. The client filters the list again to build each desk's queue, but that is presentation — this endpoint is the access control.

get.description: Separate from `/catalogue/products` because these are different numbers: a dealer lifts at trade price in whole packs, a retailer sells at face value in ones.

post.summary: Move a lifting request to the next desk
post.description:
One endpoint for every step of the chain; `action` selects.

**The server MUST take the actor from the access token and ignore any actor in the body.** An approval chain in which the client names the approver is not an approval chain — and the audit trail this whole feature exists to produce would be worthless.

**The server MUST re-check that the session holds the capability that owns the request's current stage.** Hiding a button is presentation; a request id is guessable.

200.description: The request, moved. A replayed Idempotency-Key MUST return this same body without advancing the chain a second time.

403.description: The session does not own this stage

post.summary: Find a subscriber by MSISDN or NID
post.description:
POST, not GET, because the search term is an NID or an MSISDN and a query string is written to every proxy and access log between here and CBS.

Exact match only, and deliberately so: prefix search over a subscriber base is a data-protection incident waiting to be demonstrated, and the counter always has the whole number in front of it.

query.description: A full MSISDN or a full NID. Shorter values are rejected.

get.description: Substring match, not prefix — nobody asks for a number by its first digits. Expired holds are returned to the pool by the server before the search runs; the client never expires a hold itself.

post.summary: Hold a number while the customer decides
post.description: **The server is the arbiter of this race.** Two counters can press reserve on the same number in the same second and no client can resolve that; the loser MUST receive `numberTaken`. The hold expires on the server's clock, not the client's.

200.description: The hold. A replayed Idempotency-Key MUST return this same body.

post.summary: Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token
post.description:
Called by the client **before** the current token expires, not after a 401. A retailer halfway through an e-SAF must never be bounced to sign-in because a timer ran out between two keystrokes.

It returns tokens only — never a session — so a refresh cannot quietly change who the client thinks it is.

401.description: The refresh cookie is gone or revoked. The session is over.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Generated once by the client when the mutation is queued, and reused on every retry. The server MUST return the original response for a replayed key rather than performing the work again.

DomainError.description: A domain failure. `code` maps onto the client's `error.*` keys.

Error.description: The server sends codes, never prose: prose cannot be translated and cannot be switched on.

Bilingual.description: Every server-owned display string. Bangla is the source locale.

capabilities.description: The whole access model. Navigation and route guards render from this, never from `role`.

simsOnNid.description: SIMs already registered to this NID across all operators. BTRC caps this at 15.

dateOfBirth.description: The subscriber must be 18 or older on the day of registration.

kyc.description: Regulatory. The client refuses to submit without it.

BiometricCapture.description: A browser cannot read a fingerprint scanner, so the web client only ever sends `device` — the reference returned by an external BVS capture. The React Native app sends `fingerprint`; the shape does not change.

simSerial.description: ICCID as printed on the pack.

msisdn.description: For an activation this is assigned by CBS and is news to the caller.

status.description: Port-in and ownership change complete at the regulator's pace, not the counter's.

msisdn.description: Absent for a channel that does not target a number — a scratch card is sold off the shelf and the customer enters the PIN themselves.

channel.description: The counter treats these as different products with different commission, so it travels with the request rather than being inferred from the screen the retailer opened. **The commercial distinction between flexiload, powerload and TBPS is an assumption in this document and needs confirming.**

productCode.description: For a product sale rather than airtime.

LiftingStage.description: Who is holding the request. Each name says who is waiting.

packSize.description: Demand is raised in whole packs — a dealer cannot lift 37 SIMs.

approved.description: What the zonal in-charge actually approved. Absent until approval.

LiftingEvent.description: One entry in the chain's history — the part that replaces the email thread, which is why it records the actor and not just the change.

note.description: Free text a person wrote. Not translated, and never machine-generated.

invoiceNumber.description: **Open question.** The client records an invoice number raised in ERP rather than generating one. If Teletalk One is to *generate* the invoice, this becomes a server-side sequence and the invoice desk changes shape.

approvedQuantities.description: Zonal approval may cut the quantity. Product code to approved quantity.

allocated.description: Committed to approved lifting requests but not yet dispatched.

reference.description: Settlement reference. Absent while a period is unpaid.

progress.description: Present only for a campaign the outlet is actually in.

code.description: What the customer dials. An identifier — never localised.

operator.description: Donor for a port-in, recipient for a port-out.

lastSerial.description: With firstSerial, the physical range in the box — what a shelf count is checked against. Absent for product stock, which has no serials.

lowThreshold.description: Below this the outlet should raise a requisition. Server-owned, because it varies by tier.

pending.description: Earned but not settled. The number retailers actually ring the zonal office about.

note.description: Why it is in that state, in both languages. A retailer reads this aloud.

nid.description: Never rendered unmasked by the client.

amount.description: Signed. Negative is money leaving the wallet.

variance.description: Signed per product: counted minus system.

nid.description: Never rendered unmasked by the client.

sims.description: Every SIM on this NID — what the 15-SIM ceiling is counted from.

deviceBound.description: Set by the device itself on first sign-in, not from this screen.

accuracy.description: Metres. A fix with 800 m accuracy is not evidence of a visit.

distanceMetres.description: Between the captured fix and the outlet's registered point.

photoName.description: A file name. There is no upload endpoint yet.

radiusMetres.description: How far from the registered point a transaction may be raised. 50–2000.

tier.description: Pricing band, set by the pattern in the digits rather than by the SIM.
